quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results (CFO Neil Dougherty): record results, well above the high end of the guidance range. Total company revenue of $1.600 billion was up 23% on a reported basis (acquisitions added 8 points, currency 1 point); on a core basis revenue grew 14%. Orders of $1.645 billion were up 30% reported and up 22% core. Gross margin 66.7% (up 90 basis points on favorable mix and higher-margin acquired revenue); operating expenses $628 million; operating margin 27.4%; core operating margin 28.9% on 41% core operating leverage; net income $376 million and EPS $2.17, both up 19%. Free cash flow $407 million; software and services approximately 40% of revenue and annual recurring revenue 29% of total mix. CEO Satish Dhanasekaran added that the Board has authorized a $1.5 billion stock buyback authorization.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $1.600 billion (up 23%, core 14%); orders $1.645 billion (up 30%, core up 22%); gross margin 66.7%; operating margin 27.4%; EPS $2.17

quarterly_data.signal: Communications Solutions Group revenue $1.124 billion, up 27% reported and up 16% core (gross margin 68.5%, operating margin 27.5%), with robust order growth outpacing revenue growth. Commercial communications revenue $758 million, up 33%, with growth in wireless and wireline; aerospace, defense and government $366 million, an increase of 18%. CEO: 'Wireline delivered record orders, surpassing wireless for the first time' - driven by demand for both R&D and manufacturing solutions, broad-based across compute, memory, interconnect and networking technologies, and the ninth consecutive quarter of wireline growth.
quarterly_data.figure: CSG revenue $1.124 billion (up 27%, core up 16%); commercial communications $758 million (up 33%); wireline orders a record, surpassing wireless for the first time

quarterly_data.signal: Sizing AI (CEO Satish Dhanasekaran): 'we sized our AI exposure last year in Q4 to be just about 10% of the company revenue', and on that run rate the AI business inside the wireline operation had robust order growth 'significantly above' the 30% company-average order growth. 'We've doubled the number of customers that represented that demand'; the top 2 customers at the company level were still non-AI customers. Both R&D and manufacturing grew year-over-year, and for AI 'manufacturing is becoming important to customers'. Customer set: silicon companies designing data-center chips (core customers), the manufacturing ecosystem that feeds them, an expanding hyperscaler focus, and neoclouds ('a smaller part of the business today, but growing'); more business internationally, including Southeast Asia, 'where a lot of the manufacturing installed base is'. Even so, 'we still are largely servicing, call it, the U.S.-based -- U.S. hyperscaler-based demand', with sovereign investments 'yet to come'.
quarterly_data.figure: AI just about 10% of company revenue (Q4 sizing); AI orders significantly above the 30% company-average order growth; AI customer count doubled

quarterly_data.signal: Speed transitions (CEO): 'AI workloads are driving rapid data center build-outs with 800 gig and 1.6 tera optics, alongside accelerated development of 3.2 tera'; the move to Ethernet-based AI fabrics is creating more test opportunities, and Keysight's arbitrary waveform generators and oscilloscopes are 'facilitating the move towards higher lane speeds such as 448 gig per lane to enable 3.2 tera speeds'. What used to be 'well-defined 2-, 3-year long technology refresh cycles' now happen concurrently: 'the 800 gig is being ramped and 1.6 is being accelerated in R&D and customers are talking about how do they get to 3.2', and 'the next couple of years, we see this concurrency continuing'. CSG President Kailash Narayanan: 'quite a bit of activity at this moment going on from the perspective of 1.6 terabit R&D as well as 448 gig per lane and 3.2 tera R&D'; scale-up and scale-out are both opportunities in R&D and manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: data center build-outs with 800 gig and 1.6 tera optics; accelerated development of 3.2 tera; 448 gig per lane

quarterly_data.signal: Optical interconnects (CEO): 'Rising bandwidth and power demands in AI data centers are accelerating the adoption of optical interconnects to supplement copper.' Keysight is helping optical transceiver and module suppliers ramp and design their 800-gig and emerging 1.6-terabit modules with its recently introduced Digital Communication Analyzer and Lightwave Component Analyzer products. 'Concurrently, customers are designing architectures around co-packaged optics, optical circuit switching and silicon photonics'; Keysight's tunable laser sources and polarization synthesizers provide metrology-grade measurements for silicon photonics workflows, and its workload emulation solutions help leading customers emulate real AI workload and stress conditions as clusters scale.

Outlook (CFO): Q2 FY2026 revenue $1.690 billion to $1.710 billion, 30% year-over-year growth at the midpoint; Q2 EPS $2.27 to $2.33, 35% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, on approximately 173 million weighted diluted shares; the guidance does not contemplate any impact from the Supreme Court tariff decision. Fiscal '26 base case raised: 'we now expect total annual revenue and earnings growth just above 20%' (confirmed as all-in, not organic). Visibility is strong one quarter out, the funnel visibility now extends into Q3, with less clarity for Q4; the base case is organic growth 'substantially above our long-term model even in the back half of the year'. The $375 million fiscal '26 acquisition-related revenue expectation is unchanged, as is the more than $100 million run-rate cost synergy target, weighted to late 2026 given the ERP migration timeline. With bigger deals shipping in Q2, orders and revenue are expected close together, 'either side of one'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $1.690 billion to $1.710 billion (30% growth at midpoint); Q2 EPS $2.27 to $2.33 (35% growth at midpoint); FY26 revenue and earnings growth just above 20%

quarterly_data.signal: Sales pipeline (SVP of Global Sales Steve Yoon): Q1 'was the highest quarter ever and excluding acquisitions, our second highest on record, which is unprecedented for quarter 1 for Keysight', and 'our seventh consecutive quarter of year-over-year order growth'. 'Both our total funnel and new funnel intake are at all-time highs, and our late-stage funnel is up high double digits' - one of the strongest funnels he has seen in 36 years with the company, giving strong near-term visibility and confidence into the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: the highest quarter ever (second highest on record excluding acquisitions); seventh consecutive quarter of year-over-year order growth; total funnel and new funnel intake at all-time highs

quarterly_data.signal: Supply (CEO): Keysight prepared for the scale of the business based on customer conversations last year. On memory: 'we don't have volume usage for these high-end demand, high-bandwidth kind of memories that are used in AI', so Keysight is 'not necessarily exposed to that', although memory prices are going up on the margin and were factored into the outlook and guide. Asked whether the Q2 acceleration reflects the constrained environment flagged the prior quarter easing, the CEO said it is 'largely improvements in demand'. CFO: Keysight will be 'making some investments to scale capacity'.

High-bandwidth memory and a broader AI-driven capacity expansion led to robust demand for our wafer-level test and characterization solutions.' The outlook for the year, as reflected in customers' latest technology road maps and capacity plans, has improved sequentially.

quarterly_data.signal: Electronic Industrial Solutions Group (CFO/CEO): revenue $476 million, an increase of 15% and a record, with growth across all 3 markets (general electronics, semiconductors, automotive); gross margin 62.4%, operating margin 27.2%. EISG orders grew for the third consecutive quarter, and orders and revenue both grew double digits across all 3 EISG markets. In general electronics, growth came from AI-related innovation and infrastructure investment, and the increasing complexity of high-performance PCBs (higher-density interconnects, multilayer architectures, faster speeds, tighter tolerances) is driving greater test intensity.
quarterly_data.figure: EISG revenue $476 million (increase of 15%); gross margin 62.4%; operating margin 27.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics at foundries (CEO): 'Silicon photonics programs and production time lines across major foundry customers are picking up speed and intensity', and Keysight's photonics and semiconductor expertise plus its broad R&D and production portfolio make it 'the partner of choice'.
